uses: scripts/switch_safe_hp.py, added so this comparison stops being redone wrongly
population: the 105 residue rows that no per-slot HP comparison in this program could judge
method: compare the IDENTIFIED Pokemon rather than the slot: parse the sim's switch lines for the incoming species and its HP, then require an included engine branch whose post-state has the same species at the same HP on those slots -- AND whose non-switched slot HP also agrees, via slot_hp_comparable so the check is only applied where it is valid.
a_partial_check_i_caught_before_publishi: My first pass verified only the slots that carried a switch line and reported 50. That leaves the other half of the boundary unverified -- the same partial-check error as C58's per-slot comparison, in a new place. Requiring the non-switched slot to agree as well drops it to 35. The 15-row difference is rows where the engine got the switch right and the other slot wrong.
what_the_35_are: the engine switches in the right Pokemon at the right HP and gets the other slot right too, and the row is still reported divergent. The disagreement is therefore in the component decomposition rather than the outcome -- the same shape as the non-switch instrument candidates, now measurable for the first time on this third of the residue.
what_the_70_are: the right Pokemon is on the field at the wrong HP. That is a genuine magnitude disagreement, not a presentation one, and it is not a candidate for instrument work.
no_species_mismatches: zero rows have the engine switching in a different Pokemon. Whatever else diverges, the engine's switch selection agrees with the simulator's throughout this population -- which retires drag/switch-target selection as a hypothesis for these rows.
residue_now_judged_end_to_end: 341 rows: 236 judged by per-slot comparison in earlier cycles and 105 judged here. No part of the residue is now unmeasurable for want of a valid comparison.
does_not_reach_a_pass: no code changed in the matcher or engine; unattributed stays at 341
